    "originalFile": "\\section{Method}\n\\label{sec:method}\n\n\\begin{figure*}[t]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\textwidth]{figures/pipeline.pdf}\n\\caption{Generational depth estimation pipeline. Seed documents are recursively passed through a generation operator $G_\\delta$ to produce a depth chain. Statistical features are fed to the OBD-LightGBM classifier for depth prediction.}\n\\label{fig:pipeline}\n\\end{figure*}\n\n\\subsection{Problem Formulation}\n\\label{sec:formulation}\n\nA generation operator $G_\\delta$ (LLM + decoding strategy $\\delta$) produces successive generations $X \\to Y_1 \\to \\cdots \\to Y_K$, where $Y_k = G_\\delta(Y_{k-1})$ and $Y_0 \\triangleq X$ (Figure~\\ref{fig:pipeline}).\nThis sequence forms a Markov chain.\nBy the Data Processing Inequality, $I(X; Y_1) \\geq I(X; Y_2) \\geq \\cdots \\geq 0$: the original signal degrades monotonically.\nTogether with Markov chain convergence, this guarantees a finite $\\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations are indistinguishable.\n\nWe define the operational lower bound:\n\\begin{equation}\n  \\Kempirical = \\max\\{k \\geq 1 : \\text{CI}_{\\text{lower}}^{95\\%}(\\auc_{k-1,k}) > \\theta\\},\n  \\label{eq:kstar}\n\\end{equation}\nwhere $\\theta = 0.60$ corresponds to Cohen's $h \\approx 0.20$\\footnote{$h = 2\\arcsin\\!\\sqrt{0.60} - 2\\arcsin\\!\\sqrt{0.50} \\approx 0.2014$, a ``small'' effect size by Cohen's (1988) convention.} (a conventional small-effect-size threshold) and lies well above the permutation null distribution (95th percentile $< 0.55$ across all configurations; bootstrap: 1{,}000 resamples).\nThis choice is further validated by the downstream filtering experiment (Section~\\ref{sec:filtering}), where $\\theta{=}0.60$ captures the practically meaningful boundary between actionable and non-actionable depth distinctions.\n$\\Kempirical$ varies with $\\theta$: at $\\theta{=}0.55$, $\\Kempirical{=}2$--$3$ depending on configuration ($\\Kempirical{=}3$ for Qwen variants, $\\Kempirical{=}2$ for Pythia and OLMo); at $\\theta{=}0.65$, continuation modes drop to $\\Kempirical{=}1$; at $\\theta{=}0.70$, $\\Kempirical{=}1$ universally (Section~\\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).\n\n\\subsection{Features and Classifier}\n\\label{sec:features}\n\nEach document is characterized by a 15-dimensional feature vector spanning four groups: \\emph{surprisal moments} (mean, std, skewness, kurtosis; 4~dims), \\emph{surprisal derivatives} (mean and std of first- and second-order differences, plus first-order skewness; 5~dims), \\emph{vocabulary diversity} (type-token ratio, hapax legomena ratio, self-BLEU; 3~dims), and \\emph{frequency tail statistics} (frequency kurtosis, entropy, rare token fraction; 3~dims).\nAll features are computed from token-level surprisal values via an external scorer model (full definitions in Table~\\ref{tab:s5_features}, Appendix).\nHand-crafted features enable cross-generator transfer without retraining and permit attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.\n\nWe use \\emph{Ordinal Binary Decomposition} (OBD), decomposing the $(K{+}1)$-class problem into $K$ cumulative binary sub-classifiers, each estimating $P(\\text{depth} > k \\mid \\mathbf{x})$ via LightGBM (hyperparameters in Table~\\ref{tab:s6_lgbm_params}).\nOBD achieves lower MAE than multiclass LightGBM (e.g., 0.984 vs.\\ 1.016 on Qwen-rewrite) while maintaining superior pairwise $\\auc$ (mean 0.6095 vs.\\ 0.4883 for ordinal logistic regression).\n\n\\subsection{Experimental Setup}\n\\label{sec:experimental_setup}\n\nWe evaluate five configurations spanning three model families (Table~\\ref{tab:setup}): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (rewrite and continuation modes), Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (continuation), Pythia-1.4B and OLMo-1B (continuation).\nEach uses 5{,}000 C4 seeds truncated to 256 tokens, recursively generated for $K{=}5$ iterations (30{,}000 documents per configuration).\nDefault decoding: nucleus $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$; decoding ablation covers greedy, $T{=}0.7$, and $T{=}1.2$.\nContinuation mode truncates seeds to 128 tokens and extends to 256; rewrite mode paraphrases the full text.\nEvaluation: 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by seed document; pairwise $\\auc$ as primary metric.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Experimental configurations.}\n\\label{tab:setup}\n\\begin{tabular}{llcc}\n\\toprule\n\\textbf{Config} & \\textbf{Model} & \\textbf{Mode} & $N$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nQwen-rw   & Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct & Rewrite & 5{,}000 \\\\\nQwen-cont & Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\\\\nPythia    & Pythia-1.4B            & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\\\\nOLMo      & OLMo-1B               & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\\\\nQwen-7B   & Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct   & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n",

Statistical features are fed to the OBD-LightGBM classifier for depth prediction.}\n\\label{fig:pipeline}\n\\end{figure*}\n\n\\subsection{Problem Formulation}\n\\label{sec:formulation}\n\nA generation operator $G_\\delta$ (LLM + decoding strategy $\\delta$) produces successive generations $X \\to Y_1 \\to \\cdots \\to Y_K$, where $Y_k = G_\\delta(Y_{k-1})$ and $Y_0 \\triangleq X$ (Figure~\\ref{fig:pipeline}).\nThis sequence forms a Markov chain.\nBy the Data Processing Inequality, $I(X; Y_1) \\geq I(X; Y_2) \\geq \\cdots \\geq 0$: the original signal degrades monotonically.\nTogether with Markov chain convergence, this guarantees a finite $\\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations are indistinguishable.\n\nWe define the operational lower bound:\n\\begin{equation}\n  \\Kempirical = \\max\\{k \\geq 1 : \\text{CI}_{\\text{lower}}^{95\\%}(\\auc_{k-1,k}) > \\theta\\},\n  \\label{eq:kstar}\n\\end{equation}\nwhere $\\theta = 0.60$ corresponds to Cohen's $h \\approx 0.20$\\footnote{$h = 2\\arcsin\\!\\sqrt{0.60} - 2\\arcsin\\!\\sqrt{0.50} \\approx 0.2014$, a ``small'' effect size by Cohen's (1988) convention.} (a conventional small-effect-size threshold) and lies well above the permutation null distribution (95th percentile $< 0.55$ across all configurations; bootstrap: 1{,}000 resamples).\nThis choice is further validated by the downstream filtering experiment (Section~\\ref{sec:filtering}), where $\\theta{=}0.60$ captures the practically meaningful boundary between actionable and non-actionable depth distinctions.\n$\\Kempirical$ varies with $\\theta$: at $\\theta{=}0.55$, $\\Kempirical{=}2$--$3$ depending on configuration ($\\Kempirical{=}3$ for Qwen variants, $\\Kempirical{=}2$ for Pythia and OLMo); at $\\theta{=}0.65$, continuation modes drop to $\\Kempirical{=}1$; at $\\theta{=}0.70$, $\\Kempirical{=}1$ universally (Section~\\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).\n\n\\subsection{Features and Classifier}\n\\label{sec:features}\n\nEach document is characterized by a 15-dimensional feature vector spanning four groups: \\emph{surprisal moments} (mean, std, skewness, kurtosis; 4~dims), \\emph{surprisal derivatives} (mean and std of first- and second-order differences, plus first-order skewness; 5~dims), \\emph{vocabulary diversity} (type-token ratio, hapax legomena ratio, self-BLEU; 3~dims), and \\emph{frequency tail statistics} (frequency kurtosis, entropy, rare token fraction; 3~dims).\nAll features are computed from token-level surprisal values via an external scorer model (full definitions in Table~\\ref{tab:s5_features}, Appendix).\nHand-crafted features enable cross-generator transfer without retraining and permit attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.\n\nWe use \\emph{Ordinal Binary Decomposition} (OBD), decomposing the $(K{+}1)$-class problem into $K$ cumulative binary sub-classifiers, each estimating $P(\\text{depth} > k \\mid \\mathbf{x})$ via LightGBM (hyperparameters in Table~\\ref{tab:s6_lgbm_params}).\nOBD achieves lower MAE than multiclass LightGBM (e.g., 0.984 vs.\\ 1.016 on Qwen-rewrite) while maintaining superior pairwise $\\auc$ (mean 0.6095 vs.\\ 0.4883 for ordinal logistic regression).\n\n\\subsection{Experimental Setup}\n\\label{sec:experimental_setup}\n\nWe evaluate five configurations spanning three model families (Table~\\ref{tab:setup}): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (rewrite and continuation modes), Qwen2.5-7B (continuation), Pythia-1.4B and OLMo-1B (continuation).\nEach uses 5{,}000 C4 seeds truncated to 256 tokens, recursively generated for $K{=}5$ iterations (30{,}000 documents per configuration).\nDefault decoding: nucleus $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$; decoding ablation covers greedy, $T{=}0.7$, and $T{=}1.2$.\nContinuation mode truncates seeds to 128 tokens and extends to 256; rewrite mode paraphrases the full text.\nEvaluation: 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by seed document; pairwise $\\auc$ as primary metric.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Experimental configurations.}\n\\label{tab:setup}\n\\begin{tabular}{llcc}\n\\toprule\n\\textbf{Config} & \\textbf{Model} & \\textbf{Mode} & $N$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nQwen-rw   & Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct & Rewrite & 5{,}000 \\\\\nQwen-cont & Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\\\\nPythia    & Pythia-1.4B            & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\\\\nOLMo      & OLMo-1B               & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\\\\nQwen-7B   & Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct   & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n",

63	% === Limitations (ACL required, unnumbered) ===
64	\section*{Limitations}
65	
66	Our findings are bounded by (1)~model scale ($\leq$7B, with only one 7B configuration tested; the 7B condition uses cross-scale scoring rather than self-scoring), (2)~prompt-chain rather than retrain-chain protocols (our $\Kempirical$ is a conservative upper bound on retrain-chain $\Kstar$ under monotonic-degradation assumptions), (3)~English C4 text only, (4)~four decoding strategies, (5)~threshold sensitivity ($\Kempirical$ ranges from 2--3 at $\theta{=}0.55$ to 1 at $\theta{=}0.70$ depending on configuration; all five configurations yield $\Kempirical{=}2$ at our chosen $\theta{=}0.60$), (6)~marginal boundary (Qwen-continuation 1v2 CI lower bound exceeds $\theta$ by only 0.0015; cross-scorer validation with both Pythia and OLMo scorers drops this condition to $\Kempirical{=}1$, Section~\ref{sec:transfer}), (7)~the 15D feature set yields a feature-set-specific lower bound ($\Ktheory$ may be strictly higher), (8)~the neural probe boundary is model-dependent ($\Kempirical^{\text{neural}}{=}3$ for Qwen only; $2$ for Pythia/OLMo), likely reflecting self-familiarity rather than a universal signal, and (9)~while overall feature rankings are highly consistent across models ($\rho \geq 0.85$), depth-pair-level agreement weakens at the 1v2 boundary ($\tau \approx 0.37$), indicating that per-feature contributions at the critical boundary vary across models.
67	Detailed analysis appears in Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}.
68	
69	% === Ethics Statement (ACL required, unnumbered) ===

          "-Our findings are bounded by (1)~model scale ($\\leq$7B, with only one 7B configuration tested; the 7B condition uses cross-scale scoring rather than self-scoring), (2)~prompt-chain rather than retrain-chain protocols (our $\\Kempirical$ is a conservative upper bound on retrain-chain $\\Kstar$ under monotonic-degradation assumptions), (3)~English C4 text only, (4)~four decoding strategies, (5)~threshold sensitivity ($\\Kempirical$ ranges from 2--3 at $\\theta{=}0.55$ to 1 at $\\theta{=}0.70$ depending on configuration; all five configurations yield $\\Kempirical{=}2$ at our chosen $\\theta{=}0.60$), (6)~marginal boundary (Qwen-continuation 1v2 CI lower bound exceeds $\\theta$ by only 0.0015; cross-scorer validation with both Pythia and OLMo scorers drops this condition to $\\Kempirical{=}1$, Section~\\ref{sec:transfer}), (7)~the 15D feature set yields a feature-set-specific lower bound ($\\Ktheory$ may be strictly higher), (8)~the neural probe boundary is model-dependent ($\\Kempirical^{\\text{neural}}{=}3$ for Qwen only; $2$ for Pythia/OLMo), likely reflecting self-familiarity rather than a universal signal, and (9)~while overall feature rankings are highly consistent across models ($\\rho \\geq 0.85$), depth-pair-level agreement weakens at the 1v2 boundary ($\\tau \\approx 0.37$), indicating that per-feature contributions at the critical boundary vary across models.",
          "+Our findings are bounded by (1)~model scale ($\\leq$7B, with only one 7B configuration tested; the 7B condition uses Qwen2.5-7B-Base rather than Instruct, introducing a base-vs-instruct confound---though $\\Kempirical{=}2$ consistency across this variation provides additional robustness evidence; cross-scale scoring rather than self-scoring), (2)~prompt-chain rather than retrain-chain protocols (our $\\Kempirical$ is a conservative upper bound on retrain-chain $\\Kstar$ under monotonic-degradation assumptions), (3)~English C4 text only, (4)~four decoding strategies, (5)~threshold sensitivity ($\\Kempirical$ ranges from 2--3 at $\\theta{=}0.55$ to 1 at $\\theta{=}0.70$ depending on configuration; all five configurations yield $\\Kempirical{=}2$ at our chosen $\\theta{=}0.60$), (6)~marginal boundary (Qwen-continuation 1v2 CI lower bound exceeds $\\theta$ by only 0.0015; cross-scorer validation with both Pythia and OLMo scorers drops this condition to $\\Kempirical{=}1$, Section~\\ref{sec:transfer}), (7)~the 15D feature set yields a feature-set-specific lower bound ($\\Ktheory$ may be strictly higher), (8)~the neural probe boundary is model-dependent ($\\Kempirical^{\\text{neural}}{=}3$ for Qwen only; $2$ for Pythia/OLMo), likely reflecting self-familiarity rather than a universal signal, and (9)~while overall feature rankings are highly consistent across models ($\\rho \\geq 0.85$), depth-pair-level agreement weakens at the 1v2 boundary ($\\tau \\approx 0.37$), indicating that per-feature contributions at the critical boundary vary across models.",

22	The cross-model transfer results (Section~\ref{sec:transfer}) indicate that the relative importance of depth features is largely text-intrinsic: feature rankings are highly correlated across scorers ($\rho > 0.90$), and cross-model classification retains 80--92\% accuracy (Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo: 90--92\%; broader continuation-mode pairs: 80--92\%).
23	However, absolute discriminability at the $\Kempirical$ boundary is scorer-sensitive---alternative scorers reduce Qwen-continuation $\Kempirical$ from 2 to 1, while rewrite-mode $\Kempirical = 2$ is preserved (Section~\ref{sec:transfer}).
24	At 0v1, cross-model $\auc$ exceeds 0.96 for all pairs, confirming fully transferable binary contamination detection.

broader continuation-mode pairs: 80--92\\%).\nHowever, absolute discriminability at the $\\Kempirical$ boundary is scorer-sensitive---alternative scorers reduce Qwen-continuation $\\Kempirical$ from 2 to 1, while rewrite-mode $\\Kempirical = 2$ is preserved (Section~\\ref{sec:transfer}).\nAt 0v1, cross-model $\\auc$ exceeds 0.96 for all pairs, confirming fully transferable binary contamination detection.\n\nA single depth classifier trained on one model's outputs can be deployed for texts from other models without retraining.\nTwo caveats: (1)~a nontrivial model-specific residual persists despite high transfer, and (2)~Qwen-continuation$\\leftrightarrow$OLMo retention (80--85\\%) is lower than Pythia$\\leftrightarrow$OLMo (90--92\\%), indicating that model family similarity modulates transfer.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htb]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Cross-scorer validation on Qwen-generated text. JSD values decrease approximately monotonically with depth (micro-deviations ${\\sim}$0.00002 are within noise).\nScaling beyond 7B remains open; the consistent $\\Kempirical$ across 1B--7B suggests the ``one-wash'' regime may persist even as generator quality improves.\n\n\\subsection{Cross-Model Neural Probe Analysis}\n\\label{sec:extended_neural_probe}\n\nThe neural probe (frozen-encoder MLP on each model's own hidden states) yields model-dependent $\\Kempirical^{\\text{neural}}$: Qwen-continuation achieves 2v3 $\\auc = 0.6159$ $[0.610, 0.622]$, exceeding $\\theta$ for $\\Kempirical^{\\text{neural}} = 3$; bootstrap 95\\% CIs for the accuracy difference include or border zero ($[-0.4, +10.0]$\\,pp vs.\\ GPT-5.5; $[0.0, +10.2]$\\,pp vs.\\ Claude).\nBoth LLMs achieve ${\\sim}$88\\% binary accuracy.\n\nPer-depth recall reveals convergent failure: OBD achieves 96\\% at depth-0 but only 14--22\\% at depths 2--4; GPT-5.5 achieves 77\\% (depth-0), 8--38\\% (depths 2--4); Claude: 69\\% (depth-0), 10--37\\% (depths 2--4).\nOBD's advantage derives entirely from depth-0 identification; for depths $\\geq 2$, all methods fail comparably, confirming $\\Kempirical = 2$ saturation as a data property.\nSpearman correlations are weak for all methods ($\\rho = 0.38$--$0.42$); statistical detection methods (DetectGPT~\\cite{mitchell2023detectgpt}, Binoculars~\\cite{hans2024binoculars}) optimize for the binary boundary where all approaches already succeed.\n\n\\paragraph{Sensitivity to probability merging.}\nWhen 6-class OBD probabilities are marginalized to 5 classes by merging $P(d{=}4)+P(d{=}5) \\to P(d{\\geq}4)$, accuracy rises to 44.4\\% (McNemar $p < 0.001$ vs.\\ LLMs), but the gain concentrates in depth-4 (recall: 22\\%$\\to$80\\%) while depths 2--3 collapse to 2--8\\%.\nThe raw 6-class evaluation (38.0\\%) avoids this single-class bias and is reported as the primary result.\n\n\\subsection{Broader Impact}\n\nThe practical consequence of $\\Kempirical = 2$ is a three-tier taxonomy: human-authored (depth~0), first-generation synthetic (depth~1), and deeper synthetic (depth~$\\geq 2$).\n$\\Kstar$ provides a corpus audit metric and, if prompt-chain depth signals proxy early-stage model collapse, a lightweight diagnostic without expensive retraining experiments.\n\n\\subsection{Degradation and Practical Considerations}\n\nIn our continual training experiments (Section~\\ref{sec:filtering}), all strategies degrade the base model's general capabilities (MMLU: 0.6018 $\\to$ 0.5865--0.5941; HellaSwag: 0.6821 $\\to$ 0.6638--0.6701).\nOur 100\\% synthetic setting provides an upper-bound characterization; in realistic mixed-corpus settings, degradation is proportional to the contamination fraction~\\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.\nEven under this extreme condition, $\\Kstar$-aware binary filtering reduces MMLU degradation from $-$1.53\\,pp to $-$0.77\\,pp---an approximately 50\\% reduction.\nBinary filtering at the $\\Kstar = 2$ boundary requires no per-model calibration and is universally applicable across tested configurations; combining it with distribution-matching methods (DSIR, DoReMi) is a promising direction.\n\n\\subsection{Extended Limitations}\n\\label{sec:extended_limitations}\n\n\\emph{Prompt-chain versus retrain-chain.}\nOur prompt-chain protocol holds model quality constant; real-world retrain-chains introduce additional degradation through training dynamics.\nUnder the monotonic-degradation assumption~\\cite{shumailov2024collapse}, $\\Kstar^{\\text{retrain}} \\leq \\Kstar^{\\text{prompt}}$, making our $\\Kempirical = 2$ a conservative estimate.\n\n\\emph{Threshold sensitivity.}\nAt $\\theta = 0.55$, $\\Kempirical = 3$ for Qwen-rewrite and Qwen-continuation; at $\\theta = 0.65$, all continuation modes drop to $\\Kempirical = 1$ while rewrite retains 2; at $\\theta = 0.70$, $\\Kempirical = 1$ universally (Figure~\\ref{fig:kstar_theta}).\nThe boundary is robust within a practical range but not invariant.\n\n\\emph{Boundary marginality.}\nQwen-continuation's 1v2 CI lower bound exceeds $\\theta$ by only 0.15\\,pp; Still 19 pages. The `[!htb]` didn't help either. Let me try a different approach entirely.

The fundamental issue: there's a float that's being deferred all the way to the end of the document, causing page 19 to be a float-only page. The `\clearpage` test confirmed this by forcing it to appear earlier (which created page 11 for the float, pushing everything else to 20).

Since `[!htb]` didn't work for the neural_probe table, maybe that's not the problematic float. Let me check the discussion.tex for tables:


Looking at the compile log, page 8 ends when the last section closes before conclusion starts on page 9. The neural_probe table sits at the very end of experiments_c1.tex, and even with the `!` placement specifier, if there's insufficient space on the current page, LaTeX defers it anyway.

The issue is that `[!htb]` only tries the current page and next page, but if the next page already has floats consuming the maximum allowed fraction (typically 70%), the table gets deferred further. The real fix is to make the table inline using a minipage with `\captionof`, similar to how the crossscorer table is formatted.
